edbDesc: A type of propagating disturbance. Like an ordinary wave, it carries energy and can propagate through a medium (solid, liquid, gas or plasma) or through a field such as the electromagnetic field. Characterized by an abrupt, nearly discontinuous change in the characteristics of the medium. Associated with rapid rise in pressure, temperature and density of the flow. A shock wave travels through most media at a higher speed than an ordinary wave.
title: Shock Wave
pickWhy: Mach and Salcher's 1887 photographs of shock waves around bullets are the same work as the Mach number card; the shock wave goes on that card.
